pages.text: Wind blew across the autumn field. Grandpa tied a long string to a paper kite.
Nils wanted it high in the sky, above trees and roofs. "Here we go!"
He ran, pulling the kite. Wind pushed his back. The kite fluttered behind him.
Plop. It fell onto the grass.
He ran again. The kite rose a little, then plop again.
Nils dropped the string on the grass. "It keeps falling. I won't do it."
On a stone, he watched the sky. Clouds hurried past. Not a kite in sight.
Grandpa held a handkerchief high. It fluttered only one way. "The wind comes from here."
Nils faced the wind and lifted the kite above his head. The wind swept it up!
He let out the string little by little. Above trees, above roofs flew the kite. The string pulled tight in his hand.
